Today I transplanted seedlings into the recycled hanging planters I've been building.

http://imgur.com/8J7pCv1 - STEP ONE - get out your seedlings and get ready to transplant.

http://imgur.com/MEdNwD7 - STEP TWO - realize you're an idiot and you killed all your seedlings. I'm not very patient to begin with, but I think I over-watered these guys.

http://imgur.com/oV7LX90 - STEP THREE - buy a bunch of cheap seedlings already started. These guys look nice and strong! For $1.25 each it's well worth it.

http://imgur.com/5Qcgrd2 - STEP FOUR - cut a sponge. This will be a 'sleeve' around the plant's stem to keep dirt from falling out the bottom and hold in moisture.

http://imgur.com/11xfm5z - STEP FIVE - gently extract the plant from its plastic pot. These poor guys were all rootbound (big snarl of roots in a tiny pot) so they were hard to get out!

http://imgur.com/KGYNg1t - STEP SIX - feed the plant (gently!) into the planter. The funnel shape helped me get the leaves out the mouth without too much trouble.

http://imgur.com/PLcyBMz - STEP SEVEN - transplanting is stressful and it's also supposed to be cold tonight, so tonight I'm hanging them in the pantry to recover.
